title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a Babylonian and went up to the Land of Israel, as in [Ketubot 112b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.112b.1): when he came to the border of the Land of Israel he rolled in its dust (out of his great love for the Land of Israel). There he received from all the great men of the generation, as we find Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda speaking in the name of Rabbi Yose ben Shaul in [Rosh Hashanah 24a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.24a.11) and 30a, [Moed Katan 22a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.22a.5) and [Ketubot 104a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.104a.7).[^4] Hyman suggests that perhaps Rabbi Assi, whom Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda cites in [Megillah 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.31b.6) on why one should not interrupt the curses (“My son, do not despise the Lord’s discipline”), is Rabbi Yose ben Shaul, whom Hyman says is sometimes called Rabbi Assi ben Shaul, as in [Shabbat 50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.50a.3). Hyman prefers the reading he reports from Dikdukei Soferim, with Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda speaking in Rabbi Simai’s name. In Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:8 the statement reads: “One does not interrupt in the curses. Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said: ‘Do not loathe His reproof’ — do not make it into pieces.”

Likewise Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Chanina, as in Sotah 7a in Hyman’s citation (see [Sotah 7b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.7b.3)); and he said, “It was thrown from the mouth of the group,” [Shabbat 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.3a.5) and [Pesachim 64a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.64a.10), and Tosafot on Shabbat there explain: a group of Tannaim. Hyman finds some slight support from this for the inference that he went up to the Land of Israel in Rav’s time, when there were still groups of the last Tannaim.

notes.text: Hyman’s Assi/Yose ben Shaul/Simai alternatives remain competing proposals; his inference from the last Tannaim is only slight, as supplied. קוצים קוצים is rendered in pieces, retaining the pun without invented literal thorns in the curses reading.

The inspected Megillah 31b directly reads Assi; Shabbat 50a directly names Assi ben Shaul. Neither establishes Hyman’s proposed equivalence with Yose ben Shaul or verifies the precise Dikdukei Soferim Simai reading. Shabbat 3a and Tosafot directly give the group-of-Tannaim explanation, with Tosafot also recording an alternative explanation. Hyman’s migration inference remains only slight; Ketubot 112b directly gives the dust-rolling act.

The consulted [Megillah 31b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.31b.6) names Rabbi Assi; [Shabbat 50a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.50a.3) names Rabbi Assi ben Shaul. Identifying the two, and equating them with Rabbi Yose ben Shaul, is Hyman’s suggestion.

The linked Rosh Hashanah and Moed Katan passages give a three-part chain: Chiyya bar Gamda cites Yose ben Shaul in Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi’s name. Ketubot names Chiyya and Yose in the account of the righteous who have died. The transmission in Rabbi Yose bar Chanina’s name appears at Sotah 7b in the consulted text. The dust-rolling episode does not date Chiyya’s move.
